stem: Amira has money in two savings accounts. One account earns 4% simple interest per year, and the other earns 7% simple interest per year. The equation \(0.04x + 0.07y = 910\) shows that the accounts earned a total of \$910 in interest last year, where \(x\) and \(y\) are the amounts, in dollars, in the 4% account and the 7% account, respectively. This year, Amira moves \$1,500 from the 4% account to the 7% account and makes no other changes. If the interest rates stay the same, by how many dollars will the total interest for this year be greater than last year's total?
solution: The total interest is greater by \$45.
verify:
x, y = symbols('x y')
new = Rational(4, 100)*(x - 1500) + Rational(7, 100)*(y + 1500)
old = Rational(4, 100)*x + Rational(7, 100)*y
d = simplify(new - old)
assert d == 45
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [d]
